@cygnathreadbare@retro.pizza #Debian has a long-standing reputation for reliability, which I deeply appreciate. This by-and-large hinges on all the Debian Developers (DD's), who are moreso like software "curators" (albeit all the effort needed to bend software into compliance with Debian's strict software distribution frameworks & systems, is indeed a form of software development). They make sure that nothing but high quality (or at least decent-quality) software gets in. Is slop code high quality software? Ask yourself this question. It's my observation that *most* (but not *all*) slop code is indeed low-quality. 

The Computer Scientists of the world know the difference between high- and low-quality code. Just like an architect or home inspector can look at a house, and see where building code violations are. The "normies" of the world seem to think that code that runs **whatso-fucking-ever** must be "good quality".

And even if it ends up being good quality, was the whole exercise of using LLMs worth it, for all the overhead and disadvantages, which are legion? Will it be worth it in a TCO (Total Cost of Ownership) sort of way? I think it will be a big "No" at the end of the day, but the hype is far from dead, since there's a cash volcano which hasn't stopped erupting yet. (Once it stops erupting, it'll likely be another Great Depression, as "just desserts" for all the hubris.)

Will Debian be able to retain their excellent reputation? Or will there be a whole bunch of regressions that get through? Look at all the recent outages of services like #Github  (over the last several months). Look at the sharp drop in quality in MS #Windows - they are going through a rude awakening, after all the slop code has made a ton of nasty regressions. 

**Especially look at how good AI tends to be at breaking into any online system which leaves any vulnerability on the table - even tiny mistakes**.

Will this sort of dodgy quality - which in turn has a lot to do with the integrity of the security of one's online systems - get into Debian?

#Linux #OpenSource #infosec
